doc.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21

title: Midway Gardens, Teschemacher and Ted Lewis
summary: Mugsy traces his path from Midway Gardens to Ray Miller and Ted Lewis; Pops remembers missing him in town.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Oh, I knew Tesh in 1925. When I went to Jimmy McPartland and Bud Freeman. So when I left White City, grew up in Midway Gardens, I got a hold of Tesh and Jess. We really had a swinging band at that Midway. I was considered the best band in Chicago at that time. Midway. Is that so? Oh, yeah. We used to outdraw the Trianon. You know, the big name band. Oh, really? Oh, yeah. Whose band was that? It was just a house band. House band. Right. Was Midway out on the Midway? Out near there? That was in the 60th and the Cottage Grove. Uh-huh. It was one of Lloyd Wright's creations. Frank Lloyd Wright? Yeah. Is that so? Beautiful place. It was called San Suzy Park first. Is it still there now? No, it tore that down, I think, around 1932 and 1934. Parking lot now. All those beautiful statues and everything. They're all gone. I tried to get one. The statues were the only one to give me. Where were they? Around the outside? Oh, yeah. Beautiful place. Like Lloyd Wright can only do. Yeah. I worked there for about three years. Went from there, we took our band, went over to Triangle. Tess was in a band. Jess, myself, and George Lettany. From there we went to the Mary Garden Ballroom on the north side. From Mary Garden Ballroom. I went to work with Ray Miller at the college inn. I stayed down there for a while. And I went with Ted Lewis. That was a nice sentence. That's when I first saw you, you were playing with Ted Lewis. That's it.

You know the further thing? I know the Muslim, but I didn't see the Muslim. Who was with Ted Lewis? When there ain't a town, I'm going out of that town. Or when you were playing the Palace there, I was at the Rose, and I didn't never get a chance to see you. You were playing the Palace right across the street.
